column4: The following guest appendix by Rev. Larry Low ([<u>www.LarryLow.com</u>](http://www.larrylow.com)) complements our exploration of the Holy Spirit’s role, offering practical insights on hearing God’s voice. The following guest contribution is used with permission.
column5: The following contributed appendix by Pastor Larry Low ([<u>www.LarryLow.com</u>](http://www.larrylow.com)) complements our exploration of the role of the Holy Spirit and provides practical insights into hearing the voice of God. The following guest contribution is used with permission.

column4: During prayer one morning, I asked **God** the following question: “What is the most important thing I could teach your people for the times that are heading our way?” And He answered me very quickly, and I sensed it was very urgent when He said: “**Teach them to hear My voice.**”
column5: During prayer one morning, I asked **God** the following question: “What is the most important thing I can teach Your people to prepare them for the age that is coming upon us?” The Lord answered very quickly, and I sensed a great urgency in His words. “**Teach them to hear My voice.**”

column4: When the Lord gives me a direction like that, I always pick up a pad and pencil and begin to write what little I know, or what I think I know, and the Scriptures that support it. I love doing Word studies on topics the Lord is leading me to teach. I love the anointing for preaching, but I really love to teach the Word. It is an adventure finding things that have always been there but have been overlooked.
column5: When the Lord gives such instruction, I always take a notepad and pencil and begin to write what little I know, or think I know, along with the Scripture passages that support it. I love to search the Word regarding the subjects the Lord is leading me to teach. I also love the anointing for preaching, but I truly love teaching the Word. It is an adventure to discover things that have been there all along yet overlooked.

column4: David must have longed to uncover God’s Truths, for He prayed in verse 18 of Psalm 119: “Open my eyes that I may see Wondrous things from Your law.”
column5: David must also have longed to unveil God’s truth, for he prayed this in Psalm 119:18: “Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things from Your law.”

column4: That’s what I want to see-Wondrous things from His Word.
column5: That is what I want to see - wondrous things from the Word.

column5: As I was studying and preparing the second message on discerning the voice of God, the Lord spoke to my heart as follows:

column4: The following eleven points should help you understand how the Lord will communicate with you:
column5: The following 11 points should help you understand how the Lord may speak to you:

column4: 1.  <u>Hearing God’s voice is NOT an audible sound but a KNOWING in your heart.</u>
column5: 1.  <u>Hearing God’s voice is not an audible sound, but a conviction in the heart.</u>

column4: There was one time when His Word came so clear and bold that it could have been audible. I answered Him by speaking out, it was so real. However, there was no one there but the Lord and I, so I can’t really say for sure if He spoke to me like we speak to each other.
column5: There was a time when the Word came so clearly and powerfully that it seemed like an audible voice. It was so real that I responded out loud. However, since there was no one there but the Lord and me, I cannot say for certain whether it was actually spoken with a voice as we speak to one another.

column4: There was the time when Jesus was being baptized in the river Jordan and the Father spoke: “This is My Son, in whom I am well pleased,” but even some of those there said it sounded like thunder, so I guess He could have spoken audibly to me, but for now, I want you to understand that when I say God spoke to me, it is a KNOWING in my heart more than a sound in my ear.
column5: When Jesus was baptized in the Jordan, the Father said: “This is My beloved Son; in Him I am well pleased,” yet some of those who were there said it sounded like thunder. So, while I think it is possible that the Lord spoke to me in an audible voice, for now, when I say “God spoke to me,” please understand that it is a conviction in the heart rather than a sound heard with the ears.

column4: 2.  <u>The KNOWING is NOT built by logic within your mind; however, it is a complete thought or understanding.</u>
column5: 2.  <u>That conviction is not built by the logic in your mind; rather, it is a complete thought, or understanding.</u>

column4: I have never had the Lord speak anything to me that confused me. I have never had Him speak anything to me that left me wondering ‘why.’ It is always a KNOWING with complete UNDERSTANDING. God is not the author of confusion (1 Corinthians 14:33).
column5: The Lord has never spoken anything to me that brought confusion. He has never spoken anything that made me tilt my head and ask, “Why?” It is always a conviction accompanied by complete understanding. God is not a God of confusion (1 Corinthians 14:33).

column4: 3.  <u>When He speaks, He speaks in complete thoughts.</u>
column5: 3.  <u>When the Lord speaks, He speaks in complete thoughts.</u>

column4: He never leaves us to fill in the blanks. In the twinkling of an eye, God can fill your heart with enough information to keep you preaching a lifetime. One touch from God can fill you with fire that will keep you burning eternally. He is a complete communicator.
column5: He never makes us fill in the blanks ourselves. In the blink of an eye, God is able to fill your heart with enough information to keep preaching to you for a lifetime. With a single touch from God, you are filled with a fire that will burn forever. He is a perfect communicator.

column4: 4.  <u>When God speaks to us, He NEVER DRIVES. He leads.</u>
column5: 4.  <u>When God speaks to us, He never drives us. He leads.</u>

column4: He is not a task master; He is a Shepherd. Herdsmen drive, but Shepherds lead. Jesus is the Great Shepherd of the sheep, and we are the sheep of His pasture.
column5: God is not a foreman but a shepherd. A drover drives the flock, but a shepherd leads. Jesus is the great Shepherd of the sheep, and we are the sheep of His pasture.

column4: 5.  <u>When He speaks to His children, He NEVER CONVICTS; He CONVINCES.</u>
column5: 5.  <u>When God speaks to His children, He never condemns; He gives assurance.</u>

column4: His children are those who have been Born Again (John 3:3, 5) by their confession of faith in **Jesus’** shed blood and His work on Calvary. Who wants to listen to someone who always convicts us of our wrong? I believe most of the children of **God** are afraid to hear **God** speak to them because they have been told that **God** will convict them for this or that. Look at 1 John 3:19-20. Who does it say convicts us or condemns us? It’s OUR SPIRIT or heart that condemns the child of **God**, but it is **God the Holy Spirit** that knows all things and is GREATER than our hearts. He is there to be our Comforter. Read the following Scriptures, and it will help you understand that the only ones the Holy Spirit convicts are the sinners. Romans 8:33-34 teaches us that NOTHING can come between us and **God’s** love. John 14:16, 26 teaches us that the Holy Spirit is our Comforter, not our convict-or, our Counselor, not our chastiser, our Intercessor and Helper, not our hinderer. Read also Acts 9:31 and 15:28 as examples of how the Holy Spirit (**God’s** voice) aids, comforts, and strengthens us.
column5: God’s children are those who have been born anew by confessing in faith the blood shed by **Jesus** and His work at Calvary (John 3:3, 5). Who wants to listen to someone who is always harping on our failures? I think many of **God’s** children are afraid of **God** speaking to them because they have been taught that **God** berates them about this or that. Look at 1 John 3:19-20. Who does it say is accusing and condemning us? It is our own spirit, that is, our heart, that accuses **God’s** child, but **God the Holy Spirit**, who knows all things, is greater than our hearts. The Holy Spirit is our Comforter. Read the following passages. You will see that the Holy Spirit condemns only sinners. Romans 8:33-34 teaches that nothing can come between **God’s** love and us. John 14:16, 26 teaches that the Holy Spirit is our Comforter, not an accuser; our Counselor, not a chastiser; our Intercessor and Helper, not a hinderer. Read Acts 9:31 and 15:28 as examples of how the Holy Spirit (**God’s** voice) helps, comforts, and strengthens us.

column4: 6.  <u>The voice of God can be tested so you can KNOW it is God and not your thoughts or the voice of familiar spirits.</u>
column5: 6.  <u>The voice of God can be tested. You can know that it is from God and not your own thoughts or the voice of a familiar spirit.</u>

column4: 1 John 4:1-3 instructs us to “test every spirit” so we can be sure it is from God. When you think you are hearing from God, you have the right and the responsibility to ask that voice a question (That is testing or proving the spirit.) The question to ask is: “Did Jesus Christ come in the flesh?” The one thing that familiar spirits will never admit is that Jesus came to the earth in the flesh. He was all man and all God. No false spirit or religion will admit Jesus came to this earth in the flesh and redeemed mankind from all their sin for eternity. Test the voice you hear. You must also know that God will never lead you outside His written Word, the Bible. If you are hearing something that cannot be backed up in the Bible, you are not hearing from God. Get rid of it! Test the voice you hear to see if it is from God.
column5: 1 John 4:1-3 teaches us to “test the spirits,” so that by doing so we may verify whether they are from God. When you think God is speaking, you have the right and responsibility to question that voice (that is what it means to test or prove the spirits). The question to ask is: “Did Jesus Christ come in the flesh?” The one thing a familiar spirit will never acknowledge is the fact that Jesus came to earth in the flesh. Jesus was fully man and fully God. False spirits and religions do not acknowledge that Jesus came to this earth in the flesh and redeemed humanity forever from all sin. Test the voice you hear. Also know that God will never lead you outside His written Word, the Bible. If you are hearing something that cannot be supported by Scripture, it is not from God. Cast it away! Test the voice you hear to see whether it is from God.

column4: 7.  <u>The voice of God always brings Glory to Jesus Christ.</u>
column5: 7.  <u>The voice of God always brings glory to Jesus Christ.</u>

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Voice of Heaven. He is the one here on earth to work with us, and Jesus said He will always speak only what He hears, and He will ALWAYS bring glory to Jesus (John 16:13-14). He isn’t here to bring your ministry glory or your works or the church’s programs. All those things are good, and most of them are necessary to do what we do, but the Holy Spirit will speak and bring Glory to the Person of Jesus. If you are being glorified by the voice you hear, you are not hearing God. There is a difference between being glorified and being encouraged and strengthened. The Holy Spirit will always encourage and strengthen you every time He speaks to you, even when He is correcting (guiding) you with the word. But glory is when you believe YOU are somebody. You are nobody without Jesus-HE IS THE SOMEBODY, not us.
column5: The Holy Spirit is the voice of heaven. It is the Holy Spirit who works with us on earth, and Jesus said that the Holy Spirit speaks only what He hears and always brings glory to Jesus (John 16:13-14). The Holy Spirit is not here to bring glory to your ministry, your achievements, or church programs. Those are good things and often necessary for what we are to do, but the Holy Spirit speaks and brings glory to the Person of Jesus. If the voice you are hearing results in you receiving glory, it is not the voice of God. There is a difference between receiving glory and being encouraged and strengthened. The Holy Spirit will always encourage and strengthen you every time He speaks, even when He is correcting you with the Word (in a leading way). But to “receive glory” means you believe that you are somebody. Without Jesus you are nothing—“the Somebody” is Jesus, not us.

column4: 8.  <u>God’s voice will always REVEAL something to us.</u>
column5: 8.  <u>**God’s** voice always reveals something to us.</u>

column4: Look at John 16:14. He always takes what belongs to **Jesus** and reveals it to us. The Amplified adds the words: declare, disclose, and transmit when considering the word “reveal.” **God** always discloses something to us after He declares it to us, and then by your faith, He transmits it to us. Study also 1 Corinthians 2:10 and 12.
column5: Look at John 16:14. The Holy Spirit always takes what is **Jesus’** and shows it to us. The Amplified, when considering the word “reveal,” adds the words declare, disclose, and transmit. “**God**” always discloses something to us after it has been declared, and then transmits it to us through your faith. Study 1 Corinthians 2:10 and 12 as well.

column4: 9.  <u>The voice of God will always bring peace.</u>
column5: 9.  <u>**God’s** voice always brings peace.</u>

column4: Read John 14:26 and 27, and Colossians 3:14 and 15. His voice never disturbs us. It is a voice that brings perfect peace. Inner peace is because there is a KNOWING which brings us confidence before God, which translates into perfect peace. If the voice you are listening to disturbs you, you are not hearing from God-shut it off. Jesus promised us peace, not as the world gives but as He gives us through the Holy Spirit’s comforting words and constant abiding (John 14:27).
column5: John 14:26 and 27, and Colossians 3:14 and 15. The voice of God never agitates us. It is a voice that brings perfect peace. Inner peace comes from a “knowing” that brings confidence before God, and that leads to perfect peace. If the voice you are hearing is agitating you, it is not from God—cut it off. Jesus promised to give a peace unlike what the world gives, through the comforting words and constant presence of the Holy Spirit (John 14:27).

column4: 10. <u>The voice of God ALWAYS brings TRUTH.</u>
column5: 10. <u>**God’s** voice always brings truth.</u>

column4: Read John 14:17, 26; 16:13. As a matter of fact, John 16:13 calls the Holy Spirit: “The Spirit of Truth.” God cannot lie! He is TRUTH and therefore will only speak TRUTH. I have had people say things like: “I can’t believe what I am hearing is from God. It’s too good to be true.” And maybe it is too good to be true; that’s why you MUST test the spirit by lining it up with the Word of God to be sure it is Truth. Some people just can’t believe it because what they are hearing is always positive, and they have been taught that God convicts us of error. God will only tell the TRUTH, and it will always be GOOD NEWS. The sad truth is most people only hear bad news from the voice they are listening to and never anticipate hearing good news, so when good news comes, they question it as a possible non-truth. **Truth is always good news!** It’s the **truth that** sets us free, so how could **truth** be anything but good news?
column5: Read John 14:17, 26; 16:13. In fact, John 16:13 calls the Holy Spirit “the Spirit of truth.” God cannot lie! God is truth, and therefore He speaks only truth. I have heard people say, “I just can’t believe what I’m hearing is from God. It’s too good to be true.” And it may indeed seem too good to be true; that’s precisely why you must always test the spirits against the Word of God to confirm that it is the truth. Some people say they can’t believe it because they are always hearing positive things. That is because they have been taught that God rebukes our mistakes. God speaks only truth, and it is always good news. The sad reality is that, because many people only receive bad news from the voices they are listening to and are not expecting to hear good news, when good news comes they suspect it might not be true. **Truth is always good news!** Since it is the **truth** that sets us free, how could the **truth** be anything but good news?

column4: 11. <u>The voice of **God** always LEADS US FORWARD AND UPWARD.</u>
column5: 11. <u>**God’s** voice always leads us forward and upward.</u>

column4: Read Deut. 28:1-2, Isaiah 30:21, and John 16:13
column5: Read Deut. 28:1-2, Isaiah 30:21, and John 16:13

column4: God never takes you down! He will never run you down; He only builds you up. When God speaks to you, He is speaking from the frame of reference that everything the Word says about you has already been accomplished and ACCEPTED by you. Jeremiah 33:3 says: “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you **GREAT AND MIGHTY** things which you do not know.” Does that sound like running you down or doom and gloom? There is NO doom and gloom in God, therefore He cannot tell you anything doomy or gloomy. You’ll have to tune in to the world’s news agency for doom and gloom.
column5: God will never bring you down! He will never belittle or demean you; He only builds you up. When God speaks to you, He speaks from the premise that everything the Word says about you has already been accomplished and has been accepted by you. Jeremiah 33:3 says, “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you great and mighty things which you do not know.” Does that sound like He would belittle you or speak doom and gloom? There is no doom and gloom in God whatsoever. Therefore God cannot tell you something that sounds gloomy and dark. If you want to hear doom and gloom, you will have to tune in to the world’s news outlets.

column5: > **<u>Jeremiah 29:11</u>** (NKJV)\\n>\\n> For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the LORD, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope.

column4: Now, if God THINKS good thoughts of peace, a future, and hope toward us, why would He speak otherwise? The answer is, HE WOULDN’T, and HE DOESN’T! He only leads us UPWARD and ONWARD with great hope to provide us an expected future.
column5: Now then, if God has good thoughts toward us—peace, a future, and hope—why would He say anything different? The answer is this: He never would, and He doesn't! God, with great hope, simply leads us upward and forward to give us the future we hope for.

column4: I hope this encourages you to “call upon Him” and learn how to **hear His voice**. He has great things to tell you, but He needs your listening ear before all His good things can do you any good.
column5: I hope this serves as an encouragement for you to learn how to "call on the Lord" and to **hear the Lord's voice**. God has many wonderful things to say to you, but for all those good things to benefit you, you must first listen.
